FPMC combines a learned user–candidate inner product (long-term taste) with a learned last-item–candidate inner product (first-order dynamics), trained jointly with sequential BPR. Low-rank factors share evidence across items and users rather than requiring observed counts for every transition. Fossil replaces the user embedding with a normalized sum of historical item embeddings, then adds a weighted sum of recent-item embeddings. Global plus user-specific weights control each lag; shared item factors reduce parameters. Thus recent-window extensions and additive long-/short-term combinations have established precedents. [FPMC](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf), [Fossil](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.09152)

Dirichlet-smoothed transitions use p̃(b|a)=(c_ab+τq_b)/(n_a+τ), backing sparse rows toward a background distribution q; estimating prior parameters from data gives an empirical-Bayes interpretation. Algebraically, the proposed residual is exactly λ[p̃(b|a)−q_b]. Adding it to frozen SASRec logits therefore combines SASRec’s personalized sequence representation with a globally shared, popularity-centered transition correction. This is a probability difference added to logits, requiring scale calibration—not a Bayesian posterior update of SASRec. Its distinctive element is the frozen-model correction and centering, rather than combining preferences with recency. [Transition smoothing](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02664763.2014.963525)

Sparse-support limits follow directly: an unseen source gives zero correction; small n_a produces strong shrinkage; an unobserved pair with n_a>0 receives a negative correction proportional to q_b. Counts cannot infer positive affinity for unseen pairs through latent similarity, whereas FPMC/Fossil can. Missing transitions also need not imply dislike. Before prioritizing the residual, compare validation gains against a recent-window extension and factorized transition head, reporting transition coverage and gains by support level. These are mechanism-based implications, not demonstrated benchmark improvements.
